source.objectiveEnglish: Say breakfast words clearly and greet a server or barista politely in the morning.

archivedDraft.scene: Sam enters a small café in the morning and asks about breakfast.

sourceCards.sourceSpanishNoteInternal: The accent mark puts the stress on the last syllable: ca-FÉ.
j sounds like a strong English h: HOO-go.
ch sounds like in church: LEH-cheh.
ll sounds like English y: tor-TEE-ya.
rr is a rolled r: tap your tongue several times.
h is always silent: WEH-vos.
The accent marks the stressed syllable: a-SU-car.
Stress the last syllable: meh-NOO.
Spanish a is always 'ah', as in father.
Use until about noon; after that say buenas tardes.

sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: こんにちは、お元気ですか。
sourceCards.sourceSpanishNoteInternal: Formal: use usted with staff and people you don't know.

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: My name is Sam, nice to meet you.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: サムといいます。よろしくお願いします。

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Thank you very much, see you tomorrow!
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: どうもありがとうございます。また明日！
さようなら。よい一日を。
sourceCards.sourceSpanishNoteInternal: Polite goodbye to one person you address as usted.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Sam saluda a la barista Rosa en Oaxaca: ¡Buenos días!
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Sam greets the barista Rosa in Oaxaca: Good morning!
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: サムはオアハカでバリスタのロサにあいさつします。「おはようございます！」

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Rosa
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Rosa: Hola, ¿cómo está usted?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Rosa: Hi, how are you?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: こんにちは、お元気ですか。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Sam
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Sam: Me llamo Sam, mucho gusto.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Sam: My name is Sam, nice to meet you.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: サムといいます。よろしくお願いします。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Sam lee el menú y pide un jugo de naranja.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Sam reads the menu and orders an orange juice.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: サムはメニューを読んで、オレンジジュースを注文します。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Sam también pide un café con leche.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Sam also orders a coffee with milk.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: サムは牛乳入りのコーヒーも注文します。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Sam no le pone azúcar al café.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Sam doesn't put sugar in the coffee.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: サムはコーヒーに砂糖を入れません。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Para comer, Sam pide huevos con tortillas.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: To eat, Sam orders eggs with tortillas.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 食べ物には、サムは卵料理をトルティーヤと一緒に注文します。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Rosa recomienda un churro y pan dulce.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Rosa recommends a churro and sweet bread.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: ロサはチュロスと甘いパンをすすめます。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Sam
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Sam: Muchas gracias, ¡hasta mañana!
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Sam: Thank you very much, see you tomorrow!
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: どうもありがとうございます。また明日！

lessons.speakingGoalCandidate: Breakfast words and polite morning greetings in the source Oaxaca café scene.

source.objectiveEnglish: Describe food, drinks and tables at a café with ser and estar.

archivedDraft.scene: Sam asks for a table, then checks a coffee and a sweet pastry with the server.

sourceCards.sourceSpanishNoteInternal: Use fría with feminine nouns: la leche está fría.
A man is el mesero.

sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: コーヒーはとても熱いです。
sourceCards.sourceSpanishNoteInternal: estar: a condition that can change.

sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: このテーブルは空いていますか。
パンは今日のものですか。
sourceCards.sourceSpanishNoteInternal: ser + de for origin: where or when something is from.

sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: サルサはとても辛いです。
sourceCards.sourceSpanishNoteInternal: ser: what something is like.
A woman says lista.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Daniel está en un café de Oaxaca y muchas mesas están ocupadas.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Daniel is at a café in Oaxaca, and many tables are taken.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: ダニエルはオアハカのカフェにいて、たくさんのテーブルが埋まっています。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Daniel le pregunta a la mesera: ¿Esta mesa está libre?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Daniel asks the server: Is this table free?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: ダニエルはウェイトレスに「このテーブルは空いていますか」と聞きます。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: La mesera, Rosa, dice: Sí, está libre.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The server, Rosa, says: Yes, it is free.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: ウェイトレスのロサは「はい、空いています」と言います。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Daniel
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Daniel: ¿El pan es de hoy?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Daniel: Is the bread from today?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: パンは今日のものですか。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Rosa
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Rosa: Sí, el pan dulce es fresco.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Rosa: Yes, the sweet bread is fresh.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: はい、甘いパンは新鮮です。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Daniel
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Daniel: Estoy listo para ordenar.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Daniel: I'm ready to order.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 注文が決まりました。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Rosa trae café, jugo de naranja y chilaquiles con salsa.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Rosa brings coffee, orange juice and chilaquiles with salsa.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: ロサはコーヒーとオレンジジュースとサルサのチラキレスを持ってきます。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Daniel
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Daniel: El café está muy caliente, pero el jugo está frío.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Daniel: The coffee is very hot, but the juice is cold.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: コーヒーはとても熱いですが、ジュースは冷たいです。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Daniel
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Daniel: La salsa es muy picante, pero es deliciosa.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Daniel: The salsa is very spicy, but it is delicious.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: サルサはとても辛いですが、おいしいです。

lessons.speakingGoalCandidate: Describe temperature, freshness, flavor and table availability in the source Oaxaca café scene; Spanish ser/estar has no one-to-one Japanese lesson objective.

source.objectiveEnglish: Say where you are going for breakfast, what you will order, and what you can do at a café.

archivedDraft.scene: Sam arrives at a café with outside seating and checks the choices before ordering.

sourceCards.sourceSpanishNoteInternal: Where you order or sit on a stool in a café.
Where you pay; the person there is el cajero or la cajera.

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: I'm going to order the chilaquiles.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: チラキレスを注文するつもりです。

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: We're going to have breakfast here.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 私たちはここで朝食をとるつもりです。

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Can I sit on the terrace?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: テラス席に座ってもいいですか。

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Do you make eggs to order?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 卵は好みに合わせて調理してもらえますか。
sourceCards.sourceSpanishNoteInternal: Huevos al gusto: eggs cooked the way you like.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Emma va a desayunar a una cafetería cerca del mercado.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Emma is going to have breakfast at a café near the market.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: エマは市場の近くのカフェへ朝食を食べに行くつもりです。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: En la barra, el barista Diego hace café.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: At the counter, Diego the barista makes coffee.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カウンターでは、バリスタのディエゴがコーヒーをいれています。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Emma
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Emma: Voy a pedir los chilaquiles.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Emma: I'm going to order the chilaquiles.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: チラキレスを注文するつもりです。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Emma
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Emma: Es para comer aquí, no para llevar.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Emma: It's for here, not to go.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 持ち帰りではなく、ここで食べます。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Emma
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Emma: ¿Puedo sentarme en la terraza?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Emma: Can I sit on the terrace?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: テラス席に座ってもいいですか。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Diego
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Diego: Sí, puede, y el baño está atrás.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Diego: Yes, you can, and the restroom is in the back.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: はい、大丈夫です。トイレは奥にあります。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Emma
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Emma: ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Emma: Can I pay by card?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カードで払えますか。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Diego
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Diego: Sí, puede pagar en la caja.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Diego: Yes, you can pay at the register.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: はい、レジでお支払いいただけます。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Después, Emma va a ir a la panadería por pan.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Afterward, Emma is going to go to the bakery for bread.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: そのあと、エマはパンを買いにパン屋に行くつもりです。

lessons.speakingGoalCandidate: State a breakfast destination and intended order; distinguish for-here/to-go and ask about terrace seating and card payment.
